subject: Galileo Robotics — PO requirement decision and temporary onboarding lane
messages:
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@galileorobotics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@galileorobotics.com
Date: 2028-07-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial onboarding / PO question for pilot

Hi Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re excited to spin up a short proof-of-concept with Redwood for inference on our on-device planning model. Procurement asked whether Redwood requires a formal Purchase Order for a 3-month trial (estimated spend ~$12k). Our standard is to issue a PO for most vendor spend, but we can support an invoice-only pilot if the vendor accepts a temporary exception and provides limited audit evidence.

Could you confirm Redwood’s flexibility here and the evidence needed to approve a no-PO path for a short pilot? I’ve attached a one-page summary of scope and our procurement intake form.

Attachments: Galileo-PO-Terms-Draft.pdf (pdf), Galileo-Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Aisha Kapoor
Vendor Ops — Galileo Robotics
procurement@galileorobotics.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@galileorobotics.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial onboarding / PO question for pilot

Thanks Aisha — great to meet yesterday. Short answer: we can accommodate a temporary invoice-only onboarding for a limited pilot, but Procurement will want an evidence pack and a dated approval from our procurement team.

To keep this simple, can you provide the following within 48 hours?
- Signed SOW or scope summary (one page)
- Completed onboarding checklist (you attached one; fill section B: billing entity + tax info)
- Evidence of authorized approver at Galileo (procurement email + PO waiver note)

Naomi — can you weigh in on the risk thresholds for a ~$12k pilot and whether we need a revenue holdback or net-30 invoice terms? Marissa — assigning you as PM for the onboarding checklist review.

Marcus Lin
Head of Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
[m] 415-555-0198

>

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@galileorobotics.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial onboarding / PO question for pilot

Marcus — thanks for the ping. For pilots under $25k we typically allow invoice-only with Finance approval, provided:
1) Vendor completes the onboarding checklist and provides billing/legal entity info,
2) Procurement receives an email from the vendor’s authorized procurement contact explicitly requesting a PO waiver,
3) We have a signed SOW or at minimum a one-page scope and acceptance criteria,
4) Finance confirms net-30 (or prepay) and any holdback requirements.

For a new supplier like Galileo I’d recommend a one-month invoice holdback equal to 20% of estimated spend to mitigate risk (we can release after first invoice clears). If Galileo can provide proof of purchase authority (procurement@galileorobotics.com signed by a named approver) I will fast-track the waiver.

If they prefer not to do a PO, ask them to send procurement@redwood.com a specific waiver request and include a billing contact + tax ID. I’ll review once those items are in.

— Naomi
Head of Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@galileorobotics.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial onboarding / PO question for pilot

Thanks Naomi — that list is clear. I’m attaching the updated checklist with billing entity and Tax ID filled, plus a signed one-page scope. I’ll also send a short waiver request from our Head of Procurement today (should come from procurement@galileorobotics.com).

Two quick clarification items:
- Can Redwood confirm whether the 20% holdback is deducted from the first invoice or held on account?
- For audit: is a scanned signature on the SOW sufficient, or do you need DocuSign?

Attachments: Galileo-Onboarding-Checklist.xlsx (updated), Galileo-SOW-signed.pdf

Regards,
Aisha Kapoor
Vendor Ops — Galileo Robotics

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@galileorobotics.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T10:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial onboarding / PO question for pilot

Looping back after quick review of the checklist and SOW. Checklist looks complete; legal entity + tax ID present. SOW contains clear acceptance criteria for the pilot (latency SLAs and token caps).

Naomi — from an onboarding perspective we’re comfortable if Finance accepts net-30 with a 20% holdback on the first invoice. If that’s approved I’ll create the trial seat and tag the account as "pilot: galileo-2028" and note the waiver in the vendor record.

Aisha — DocuSign would be preferred but not mandatory for this pilot; a scanned signature is acceptable if the waiver email originates from an authorized procurement address. If you can send DocuSign within the week that would close the loop for legal.

Next steps:
- Aisha to send procurement waiver email (procurement@galileorobotics.com) addressed to procurement@redwood.com
- Naomi to confirm Finance holdback approach (deduct vs. escrow)
- Marissa to provision pilot once waiver confirmed

Thanks — Marissa
Program Manager, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@galileorobotics.com>
Date: 2028-07-24T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial onboarding / PO question for pilot

Confirming — Finance will accept net-30 with a 20% deduction applied to the first invoice (credit issued on the second invoice after reconciliation). We prefer deduction for operational simplicity; legal is fine with a scanned SOW for pilots under $25k.

Aisha — please send the waiver email and copy the named procurement approver. Once we get that, Marissa can provision and I’ll record the waiver approval in the vendor record.

— Naomi
Head of Procurement Ops
Redwood Inference
